title: Kitchen Organization Basics
subtitle: Four zones in one direction, and a station you set up the same way twice.
objectives: Explain why the zones are ordered that way
Describe how to set up a workstation

cards.title: A kitchen is laid out, not just filled
cards.text: Almost every kitchen accident and every slow dinner comes from the same thing: crossing your own path.

cards.title: Four zones, one direction
cards.text: Food moves through a kitchen in one line.
points: **Store** — fridge, pantry, cupboards.
**Wash** — sink, drainer, bin.
**Prep** — board, knives, clear surface.
**Cook** — stove, oven, pans.

cards.title: Tap a zone
cards.text: Tap each zone, then tap the walk. The order is the point.

question.text: Why does wash sit between store and prep?
question.explain: The zones follow what the food does.

cards.title: One square metre, set up the same way every time
cards.text: A set-up you repeat is a set-up you stop thinking about.
points: **Board in the middle**, damp cloth underneath.
**Knife on your dominant side**, blade away.
**Bowl for scraps** on the other side.
**Finished pieces in a tray**, not left on the board.

question.text: What goes under the chopping board?
question.explain: A board that slides is a board that cuts you.

cards.title: It is a time strategy, not tidiness
cards.text: The washing-up happens in time you were going to waste anyway.
points: **Something is always simmering or resting.**
**That is the window.**
**Wipe the board between raw and ready-to-eat** — not optional.
**A kitchen cleaned at the end** takes twice as long.

cards.title: Zoning is inventory management
cards.text: Every game you play solves the same problem.
points: **Things you use often go where you reach first.**
**Things you rarely use go deep.**
**Walking across the map for one item** is wasted time.
**A good kitchen is a good hotbar.**

cards.title: A pit box has zones too
cards.text: Nobody in a pit crew crosses another's path. It is designed out.
points: **Tyres on one side. Fuel on the other.**
**Every tool has a position**, not a drawer.
**Two seconds saved per stop** wins races.
**Same principle in a kitchen**, slower stakes.

cards.title: Lay the screws out in order
cards.text: Anyone who has opened a fan knows this one.
points: **Screws in a line**, in the order you removed them.
**Panels stacked the way they came off.**
**Reassembly becomes reading backwards.**
**Same habit, different bench.**

cards.title: What to remember
points: Store, wash, prep, cook — one direction, no crossing back.
Set your workstation up identically every time.
Damp cloth under the board, knife on your dominant side.
Clean in the gaps, not at the end.

quiz.text: Which zone comes first for food arriving?
quiz.explain: It should not cross the room to be used.
And it sits off the walkway.
Prep with no space is where accidents happen.
quiz.objective: Explain why the zones are ordered that way

quiz.text: Why is the cook zone kept off the walkway?
options: So nobody walks past a hot pan
quiz.explain: Design it out rather than warn about it.
quiz.objective: Explain why the zones are ordered that way

options: On your dominant side, blade away

quiz.explain: A crowded board is a slow board.
quiz.objective: Describe how to set up a workstation

quiz.explain: It is a time strategy: the washing-up fits in the waiting.

quiz.text: When is the board wiped without exception?
Zoning a kitchen is most like…
quiz.explain: Often-used things where you reach first.

quiz.explain: The same habit as a workstation set-up.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 2 TLE. The week's claim is that almost every slow or dangerous kitchen is one where people cross their own path, so the zones are drawn as a plan with the walk between them rather than listed. The workstation card is deliberately specific — board centred, damp cloth under it, knife on the dominant side, tray for finished pieces — because a repeated set-up is one he stops having to think about. Clean-as-you-go is argued as a time strategy rather than a tidiness rule, with the one exception that is genuinely about safety: wiping between raw and ready-to-eat. Three lenses say the same thing from the hotbar, the pit box and the workbench.
discussion: Ask him to name the four zones in order.
Ask why the cook zone is off the walkway.
Ask him to set the station up and then explain each position.
Ask what a pit crew and a kitchen have in common.
extension: Have him redraw your actual kitchen as four zones and say what he would move.
Have him cook one dish cleaning only in the waiting time.
misconceptions: "Any surface will do for prep." It needs the biggest clear space.
"Clean up at the end." It takes twice as long.
"Wiping the board is about mess." Between raw and ready-to-eat it is safety.
